we_do_better: Techniques vs. tools distinction — we separate reusable methods (Skills) from products (Tools), which no competitor does; uniquely valuable for practitioners
Source transparency — video quality badges, low-quality flags, and endorsement counts let users judge credibility at a glance; competitors show no provenance
MCP/connector tracking — dedicated Connectors tab covering MCP servers is a niche no competitor addresses
Live RSS news feed merged with video-sourced news, covering 50+ authoritative AI sources alongside the playlist
Self-improvement system and open audit trail (merge log, deleted skills, suggestion queue) — competitors are static catalogs that never explain their curation choices
Fully free, open-source, no ads, no paywall
they_do_better: Visual thumbnails and tool logos — Future Tools, Product Hunt AI, and Toolify show product images; our wall of text cards is harder to scan quickly
Item-count badges per category — Future Tools and TAAFT display count per filter tab; users immediately know scope before clicking
Simultaneous multi-axis filtering — Toolify lets users filter by category + pricing + rating at once; we only support single-axis category filter per tab
Hero section and featured/trending slots — all four competitors surface a 'start here' section; we drop visitors into an unlabelled card list
Sort controls — competitors offer newest / top-rated / most-popular sort; our Skills and Tools tabs only sort by quality score with no user control
User-generated signals — Product Hunt shows upvotes and comments; TAAFT shows verified-user saves; our popularity is editorial (video endorsement counts), not crowd-sourced
borrow_next: Add item-count badges to tab buttons (e.g. 'Skills (69)', 'Tools (121)') — one line of JS per tab, high discoverability signal at zero cost; read from loaded JSON arrays, not stale status.json
Add a sort toggle (Quality | Mentions | Newest) to the Skills and Tools tabs — ~15 lines of JS, eliminates the main gap vs Toolify/Future Tools for power users

Add a 2-sentence 'What is Excavatortron?' tagline beneath the H1, and pin the top-3 starred skills to the top of the Skills tab as a 'Featured' strip — teaches new visitors what they're looking at without a tutorial

findings.detail: TODAY = datetime(2026, 6, 3, tzinfo=timezone.utc) is hardcoded at module level. compute_age_months() uses this frozen date, so all recency penalties after June 3 2026 are wrong — videos appear progressively older than they are. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Replace with datetime.now(timezone.utc) computed inside compute_age_months at call time, not at module level.

findings.detail: load_json and save_json open files without encoding='utf-8'. Hebrew transcripts and Unicode tool names will cause UnicodeDecodeError/UnicodeEncodeError on non-UTF-8 locale runners. src/fetch.py uses encoding='utf-8' consistently; analyze_batch.py does not. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add encoding='utf-8' to every open() call in load_json (L153) and save_json (L161). Also fix the remaining bare open() calls at lines 402, 725-726, 747-748.

findings.detail: process_video.py has its own duplicated load_json/save_json (lines 16–28) with the same missing encoding='utf-8' as analyze_batch.py. _write_skill_md() at line 318 also opens SKILL.md output with bare open(). All three fail on Hebrew-sourced or Unicode-named content. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add encoding='utf-8' to load_json (L19), save_json (L26), and _write_skill_md (L318) in process_video.py. Consolidate load_json/save_json into a shared src/utils.py to prevent this divergence recurring.

findings.detail: no_transcript=53, new_found=53 — 100% transcript fallback rate again this run (down from 78 but still 100%). Every new video fell back to description or title. The broad except-all in fetch_transcript() silently swallows failures. The pending backlog is now cleared so absolute numbers fell, but the underlying transcript-fetch failure is not fixed.
findings.suggestion: Log the exception at WARNING before falling back. Add a health flag: if no_transcript / new_found > 0.5, set status['transcript_health'] = 'degraded' and show an amber dashboard banner. Verify youtube-transcript-api version compatibility.

findings.detail: describe_tool() returns a hardcoded category-keyed string regardless of video content. 36 of 121 tools (29.7%) still have template descriptions — down from 43% last run, but the root cause (describe_tool()) is still unfixed. Every new analyze_batch.py run injects more fakes. The Claude-driven CLAUDE.md path extracts real descriptions, so skills.json is clean, but tools.json has stale templates from earlier batch runs.
findings.suggestion: Replace describe_tool() with extraction from the transcript: use the 1–2 sentences in the video that most concisely describe what the tool does. If no sentence qualifies, set description to null and show 'Description not yet extracted' in the dashboard.

findings.detail: 'Anthropic' is catalogued as a tool (6/10, 74× mentions) with description 'Anthropic is an AI tool by Anthropic. It enhances productivity through AI-powered features and automation.' Anthropic is the company, not a product. Its tool-card is misleading and inflates the tools count. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Remove the 'anthropic' tool entry; fold its endorsement_video_ids into the 'claude' tool entry. Add to improvement_suggestions.json as a safe_auto merge (already queued as suggestion b9bfdaf0ef).

findings.detail: 'Openai' (incorrect casing, should be 'OpenAI') is catalogued as a tool (46× mentions) with a template description. OpenAI is the company; ChatGPT, GPT-4, etc. are its products and already have separate entries. The entry both duplicates credit and shows wrong branding. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Remove the 'openai'/'Openai' tool entry; fold its endorsement_video_ids into 'chatgpt'. Already queued as suggestion b9bfdaf0ef.

findings.where: data/tools.json — 36 of 121 entries (29.7%) have template descriptions
findings.detail: 36 tool entries use describe_tool() template patterns ('enhances productivity through AI-powered features', 'assists with software development', 'automates workflows', etc.). This is down from 38/89 (43%) last run — the Claude CLAUDE.md path has added 32 new tools with real descriptions — but the root cause (describe_tool() in analyze_batch.py) is still unfixed and will re-infect the catalog if analyze_batch.py ever runs.
findings.suggestion: Fix describe_tool() in src/analyze_batch.py to extract real content from transcripts (see finding e5a3f8b2c7). The improve stage's fill_missing_summaries module should back-fill existing template descriptions where transcripts are available.

findings.detail: analyze_batch.py still generates skill records with three hollow template fields: use_case ('Using {tool} for {category} tasks.'), output ('{tool} produces {category}-focused outputs.'), and relevance ('{tool} is featured as an AI tool in this video.'). HOWEVER: skills.json now has 69 real, non-template skills (0% template fields) because the Claude CLAUDE.md path generates real content. The code bug remains but has no impact on current data. If analyze_batch.py runs it will re-introduce templates.
findings.suggestion: Extract use_case and relevance from the transcript (same approach as extract_tips). If no qualifying sentence is found, use null/empty rather than a template string.

findings.where: data/daily_news.json (7 empty) + data/weekly_news.json (109 empty) + data/monthly_news.json (157 empty)
findings.detail: 273 video news entries now have empty summaries showing '(summary pending)' — WORSENED from 169 last run. The weekly backlog grew from 75→109 and monthly from 91→157. With no_transcript=100% this run, every newly-classified news entry has no real transcript to summarize from. Neither fill_missing_summaries nor the analyze stage is clearing the backlog.
findings.suggestion: The improve stage's fill_missing_summaries module should generate 1-sentence summaries from available description text for no-transcript videos. Address the transcript-failure root cause (finding 8a1b5c4d6e) so future fetches have real content.

findings.detail: MCP connector detection uses a hardcoded list of only 8 specific string patterns (filesystem, browser, github, postgres, sqlite, memory, slack, google drive). Any other MCP server mentioned in a video is silently ignored. CLAUDE.md Step 8 specifies exhaustive MCP hunting. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Broaden detection: capture any pattern matching 'npx .+-mcp', 'uvx .+-mcp', 'mcpServers', 'smithery', or 'mcp.so' in the text as a generic MCP connector, extracting the name from the matched string.

findings.detail: Slash-command regex r'/[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{1,20}\b' matches URL path segments (/api, /v1), prose slashes, and file paths. The exclusion list only blocks 14 single-character tokens. NOTE: current commands.json (14 entries) shows only real commands (/ultra-plan, /goal, /agents etc.) because the Claude CLAUDE.md path generates them correctly — but if analyze_batch.py runs on raw text it will accumulate false positives. Code bug still present.
findings.suggestion: Add a context requirement: only record a slash command if it appears adjacent to known AI tool names or a command-demonstration phrase. Extend blocklist to path prefixes (/api, /v1, /v2, /src, /static, /docs).

findings.detail: The tool is stored as 'Chatgpt' (wrong casing) instead of the correct brand name 'ChatGPT'. This is the 3rd most-mentioned tool (114 mentions) and the casing error appears for every visitor. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Rename name to 'ChatGPT' in data/tools.json. Already queued as suggestion 253d755074.

findings.detail: fetch_playlist_videos calls request.execute() with no retry or error handling for YouTube API quota exhaustion (HttpError 429/503). If the quota is hit mid-pagination (playlist has 1054+ items across ~22 pages), the function raises an unhandled exception and the entire fetch run fails. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Wrap request.execute() in a retry loop with exponential backoff for 429/503, up to 3 attempts, before re-raising.

findings.detail: write_skill_md() in both analyze_batch.py (L402) and process_video.py (L318) opens SKILL.md output files with bare open() — no encoding='utf-8'. Additionally, main() in analyze_batch.py opens pending JSON files (L725-726, L747-748) without encoding. Hebrew content or Unicode tool names will cause UnicodeEncodeError on non-UTF-8 runners. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add encoding='utf-8' to all remaining open() calls: analyze_batch.py lines 402, 725-726, 747-748 and process_video.py line 318.

findings.detail: In git_commit_push(), the retry loop calls git pull without checking its return code. If pull fails (merge conflict, auth failure), code continues and retries push on a broken state, exhausting all 3 retries without diagnosis. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Check the return code of git pull: if pr2.returncode != 0, log stderr and return early. Example: if pr2.returncode != 0: return f'pull failed: {pr2.stderr[:100]}'.

findings.detail: Tab buttons show no item count. Competitors (Future Tools, TAAFT) display per-category counts. The dashboard now shows 69 skills and 121 tools but the nav buttons say nothing. The header counter 'Total skills' shows the stale status.json value (38) rather than the actual 69. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: After loading each tab's data in the init() async block, inject item counts into nav buttons from loaded JSON arrays (not status.json): e.g. 'Skills (69)', 'Tools (121)', 'Connectors (18)'. ~10 lines of JS. Already queued as suggestion 3693c44f40.

findings.detail: Skills and Tools tabs have no sort control. Users can only filter by category; they cannot sort by newest, mentions, or reverse quality. All four benchmark competitors offer multi-axis sort. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add a sort <select> or pill-toggle above each card list: Quality (default) | Mentions | Newest. Client-side sort on the already-loaded array. ~20 lines of JS. Already queued as suggestion 72e04d9c61.

findings.detail: No hero tagline explains what Excavatortron is. First-time visitors see 'Excavatortron — AI Skills Tracker' and a search box with no context. All four competitors have a 2-3 sentence value proposition above the fold. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add one sentence beneath the subtitle: 'Tracks AI techniques, tools, models, and MCP connectors extracted from a curated YouTube playlist — updated automatically, quality-scored, and searchable.'

findings.detail: Inline Python in both workflows uses datetime.datetime.utcnow() which is deprecated in Python 3.12+ and will emit DeprecationWarning. When GitHub Actions upgrades to Python 3.13+, this may become a hard error. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Replace datetime.datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + 'Z' with datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat() in both workflow inline scripts.

findings.detail: renderAlert builds el.innerHTML = msg where msg contains raw HTML tags hardcoded in JS alongside esc(status.token_hint). The esc() call protects the dynamic value but the pattern (mixing safe-markup with partially-escaped content) is fragile — a future maintainer adding another dynamic field may forget esc(). Data comes from repo-committed JSON (low external risk) but the pattern is worth fixing. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Build the alert using DOM methods (createElement, textContent) rather than innerHTML, or create a dedicated safe-template function that always escapes dynamic values.

findings.detail: main() always sorts pending records newest-first (reverse=True at line 735), regardless of the workflow's order instruction. The analyze.yml workflow outputs 'order=oldest_first' for normal runs but analyze_batch.py ignores this entirely — has no --order parameter. CLAUDE.md Step 1 specifies oldest_first as the normal default. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add an --order argument to analyze_batch.py (default 'oldest_first'). Sort ascending when oldest_first. Pass the workflow plan step's order value to the script via argument or env var.

findings.detail: /tmp/sorted_pending.json is written on first call and reused on subsequent calls within the same runner. GitHub Actions may reuse warm runners for back-to-back analyze jobs. If the file exists from a previous run, newly added pending videos are absent. The file is never deleted. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Delete /tmp/sorted_pending.json at the start of every main() invocation before checking if it exists, or unconditionally regenerate it on each call.

findings.detail: status.total_skills is 38 but skills.json actually contains 69 skills — now a 45% undercount, WORSENED from 73% last run (10 vs 38). The dashboard 'Total skills' counter shows 38, not 69. analyze_batch.py never updates this field after appending skills. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: In process_video() (analyze_batch.py / process_video.py), after saving skills.json, add: status['total_skills'] = len(skills_data['skills']). Or compute it in the dashboard from the loaded skills array rather than trusting status.total_skills.

findings.detail: NEW FINDING: index.json has 110 slug entries but skills.json has only 69 skills — 41 phantom slugs exist in the index with no corresponding skill record. When analyze_batch.py processes a video and finds a tool whose slug matches a phantom index entry, it attempts to look up the skill: `next((s for s in skills_data['skills'] if s['slug'] == slug), None)` returns None, and the merge branch falls through without appending the new skill. Result: those 41 tools are silently blocked from ever being added to skills.json even when they appear in new videos.
findings.suggestion: On startup in main(), after loading index.json, reconcile it against skills.json: remove any slug from index_data that has no matching entry in skills_data['skills']. One pass: {s['slug'] for s in skills_data['skills']} → drop phantom keys from index_data and re-save. Run this reconciliation once immediately to fix the current 41 phantom entries.

findings.detail: NEW FINDING: create_news_summary() generates generic fallback text for videos with no real description: '{title}. AI content video featuring tools and techniques.' With 100% transcript fallback rate (all 53 new videos this run had no real transcript), every news summary written this run is either generic filler or description-scraped text with no human-readable insight. This is the direct engine cause of the 273 empty/low-quality news summaries.
findings.suggestion: For no-transcript videos, generate a 1-sentence summary from the video title and any available tags/description text. Even a concise 'Video about {tools_found}: {title}' is more useful than the generic template. Also add a 'summary_quality' field ('full'/'description'/'title_only') so the news tab can badge thin summaries.
